questions.sampleA2:
I study English at school.

I like it, and it is interesting.

I study grammar and vocabulary because I want to speak English well.
questions.sampleB1:
I study English language and literature at university.

I think it's a very interesting subject because I enjoy reading books and learning about different cultures.

For example, we are reading Shakespeare this semester, which is quite challenging but also very rewarding.

I also study grammar and writing.
questions.sampleB2: Well, to be honest, right now I'm studying economics at university, and it really keeps me on my toes. We deal with everything from finance to marketing, so there's never a dull moment. I suppose what I enjoy most is how practical it is, and hopefully it'll open plenty of doors once I graduate.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men maktabda ingliz tilini o'qiyman.

Menga u yoqadi va u qiziqarli.

Men grammatika va lug'atni o'qiyman, chunki men ingliz tilida yaxshi gapirishni xohlayman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men universitetda ingliz tili va adabiyotini o'qiyman.

Menimcha, bu juda qiziqarli fan, chunki men kitob o'qishni va turli madaniyatlar haqida bilishni yaxshi ko'raman.

Masalan, biz bu semestrda Shekspirni o'qiyapmiz, bu ancha qiyin, lekin juda foydali ham.

Men grammatika va yozishni ham o'qiyman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men hozirda Atrof-muhit fanlari bo'yicha daraja olmoqdaman.

Bu biologiya, kimyo va yer fanlarini birlashtirgan holda dolzarb ekologik muammolarni hal qilishga qaratilgan juda qiziqarli soha.

Men bu mutaxassislikni tanladim, chunki iqlim o'zgarishi meni juda tashvishga soladi va barqaror yechimlarni topishga hissa qo'shmoqchiman.

O'quv dasturi juda talabchan, ko'plab dala ishlari va ma'lumotlarni tahlil qilishni o'z ichiga oladi, lekin men buni juda rag'batlantiruvchi deb bilaman.

Oxir-oqibat, men tabiatni muhofaza qilish yoki qayta tiklanadigan energiya sohasida ishlashga umid qilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - What do/did you study?
sentenceStarters: "I'm currently studying..." - "Men hozirda ... o'qiyapman"
"I graduated with a degree in..." - "Men ... bo'yicha diplom oldim"
"My major is/was..." - "Mening mutaxassisligim..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'm currently studying English Linguistics at the National University of Uzbekistan. It's a four-year bachelor's program that primarily focuses on language theory, phonetics, and translation studies.
Previously, I completed my secondary education at a specialized school where I had an intensive curriculum in foreign languages. This really sparked my interest in pursuing higher education in this field.
As they say, "Knowledge is power" – and I believe studying languages opens many doors.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men hozirda O'zbekiston Milliy Universitetida ingliz tilshunosligini o'qiyapman. Bu to'rt yillik bakalavr dasturi bo'lib, u asosan til nazariyasi, fonetika va tarjima tadqiqotlariga qaratilgan.

Ilgari, men ixtisoslashtirilgan maktabda o'rta ta'limni tugatganman, u yerda chet tillari bo'yicha intensiv o'quv dasturiga ega edim. Bu menga ushbu sohada oliy ma'lumot olishga bo'lgan qiziqishimni juda ham oshirdi.

Aytishlaricha, "Bilim - kuch" – va menimcha, tillarni o'rganish ko'plab imkoniyatlar eshigini ochadi.

questions.prompt: Why do/did you want to study that?
questions.sampleA1: I like. Study English. Good for me. Happy.
questions.sampleA2: I want study English because it's important. My job needs English and I like travel. I want to talk to people in other countries, and English is good for that.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I wanted to study marketing because I think it's a really interesting subject. In my opinion, it's important for businesses to understand their customers. Also, I'm quite a creative person, so I thought marketing would be a good way to use my creativity. For example, I enjoy coming up with new ideas for advertising campaigns.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the thing is, I've always been fascinated by how money and markets work, so economics felt like a natural fit. To be honest, I also wanted a subject that would stand me in good stead when it comes to finding a job. And I suppose I just love getting to grips with what makes the world tick.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga yoqadi. Ingliz tilini o'rganish. Men uchun yaxshi. Xursandman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men ingliz tilini o'rganmoqchiman, chunki bu muhim. Mening ishim ingliz tilini talab qiladi va men sayohat qilishni yaxshi ko'raman. Men boshqa davlatlardagi odamlar bilan gaplashmoqchiman va ingliz tili buning uchun yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, men marketingni o'rganmoqchi edim, chunki bu juda qiziqarli mavzu deb o'ylayman. Mening fikrimcha, bizneslar o'z mijozlarini tushunishi muhim. Bundan tashqari, men ancha ijodkor odamman, shuning uchun marketing mening ijodkorligimni ishlatish uchun yaxshi yo'l bo'ladi deb o'yladim. Misol uchun, menga reklama kampaniyalari uchun yangi g'oyalar o'ylab topish yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men atrof-muhitshunoslikni o'rganishni tanladim, chunki men doimo sayyoramizning holatidan chuqur tashvishlanganman. Menimcha, agar biz iqlim o'zgarishi va ifloslanish kabi muammolarni samarali hal qilishni istasak, atrof-muhitimizni boshqaradigan murakkab tizimlarni tushunish juda muhim. Bundan tashqari, meni bu sohaning fan, siyosat va iqtisodiyot kesishmasini o'rganishga imkon beradigan fanlararo tabiati o'ziga tortdi. Oxir-oqibat, men sog'lom kelajak uchun barqaror yechimlarni topishga hissa qo'shishga intilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Why do/did you want to study that?
idioms: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step - "Ming millik sayohat bitta qadam bilan boshlanadi"
sentenceStarters: "There are several reasons why I chose..." - "... ni tanlashimning bir necha sabablari bor"
"I've always been fascinated by..." - "Men doim ... dan qiziqardim"
"What motivated me was..." - "Meni motivatsiya qilgan narsa..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several reasons why I chose to study English Linguistics. Primarily, I've always been genuinely fascinated by how languages work and how people communicate across cultures.
Additionally, English is the global lingua franca, so mastering it opens up countless career opportunities in international business, diplomacy, and education.
I was also inspired by my English teacher in school who showed me how beautiful and complex language can be. "A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step" – and learning English was my first step toward a global career.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ingliz tili lingvistikasini o'rganishni tanlaganimning bir nechta sabablari bor. Asosan, men tillar qanday ishlashi va odamlar madaniyatlararo qanday muloqot qilishlari meni doim chinakam qiziqtirib kelgan.

Bundan tashqari, ingliz tili global lingua franca hisoblanadi, shuning uchun uni mukammal o'zlashtirish xalqaro biznes, diplomatiya va ta'lim sohalarida son-sanoqsiz martaba imkoniyatlarini ochadi.

Maktabdagi ingliz tili o'qituvchim ham meni ilhomlantirgan, u tilning naqadar go'zal va murakkab bo'lishi mumkinligini ko'rsatdi. "Ming milyalik sayohat birinchi qadamdan boshlanadi" – va ingliz tilini o'rganish mening global martaba sari qo'ygan birinchi qadamim edi.

questions.prompt: What subject do you enjoy studying most?
questions.sampleA2:
I like history.

It is interesting and I like the stories.

I don't like maths because it is difficult.
questions.sampleB1:
I enjoy studying biology the most.

I think it's really interesting to learn about how living things work.

For example, learning about the human body is fascinating.

Also, I want to be a doctor, so it's important for my future.
questions.sampleB2: Honestly, out of all my subjects, I get the biggest kick out of microeconomics. I know that might sound a bit nerdy, but I find it genuinely eye-opening how small decisions add up to shape whole markets. The thing is, it's like solving a puzzle — everything just falls into place. I could talk about it for hours.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menga tarix yoqadi.

U qiziqarli va menga hikoyalar yoqadi.

Menga matematika yoqmaydi, chunki u qiyin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men biologiya fanini o'rganishdan eng ko'p zavqlanaman.

Menimcha, tirik mavjudotlar qanday ishlashini o'rganish juda qiziqarli.

Masalan, inson tanasi haqida o'rganish juda hayratlanarli.

Shuningdek, men shifokor bo'lishni xohlayman, shuning uchun bu mening kelajagim uchun muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men tarixni eng qiziqarli fan deb bilaman.

Garchi ba'zilar uni shunchaki sanalarni yodlash deb hisoblashi mumkin bo'lsa-da, menimcha, u hozirgi kunga bebaho tushunchalar beradi.

O'tmishni tushunish orqali biz hozirgi voqealarning murakkabligini yaxshiroq anglashimiz va xatolarni takrorlashdan qochishimiz mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, turli tarixiy nuqtai nazarlarni tahlil qilish turli madaniyatlar va jamiyatlarni yanada nozik tushunishga imkon beradi.

U tanqidiy fikrlashni rag'batlantiradi va yanada xabardor dunyoqarashni rivojlantirishga yordam beradi.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - What subject do you enjoy studying most?
idioms: The pen is mightier than the sword - "Qalam qilichdan kuchli"
sentenceStarters: "Among all my subjects, I particularly enjoy..." - "Barcha fanlarim orasida men ayniqsa ... ni yoqtiraman"
"I find it extremely rewarding when..." - "... bo'lganda bu juda qoniqarli"
"What I love most about it is..." - "Men eng ko'p yoqtiradigan narsa..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Among all my subjects, I particularly enjoy studying Stylistics and Literary Analysis. It's incredibly fascinating to analyze how writers use language to create meaning and evoke emotions.
I find it extremely rewarding when I can identify literary devices like metaphors, irony, and symbolism in texts. It's like solving a puzzle – each text has hidden layers waiting to be discovered.
Moreover, this subject helps me improve my writing skills and express myself more eloquently. As they say, "The pen is mightier than the sword".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Barcha fanlarim orasida, men ayniqsa Stilistika va Adabiy Tahlilni o'rganishdan zavqlanaman. Yozuvchilar tilni ma'no yaratish va his-tuyg'ularni uyg'otish uchun qanday ishlatishini tahlil qilish juda hayratlanarli.

Matnlarda metafora, ironiya va ramziylik kabi adabiy vositalarni aniqlay olganimda, o'zimni juda mamnun his qilaman. Bu jumboqni yechishga o'xshaydi – har bir matnda yashirin qatlamlar bor, ularni kashf etishni kutib turadi.

Bundan tashqari, bu fan menga yozish mahoratimni oshirishga va o'z fikrlarimni yanada ravonroq ifoda etishga yordam beradi. Aytishlaricha, "Qalam qilichdan kuchliroq".

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1:
I see people.

They walk.

I see a plane.
questions.sampleA2:
I see people walking.

In one picture, they are on the street.

And in the other picture, they are in a museum, I think.

It is a big plane.
questions.sampleB1:
In the pictures, I can see people walking in two different places.

The first picture shows some young people walking on a street, maybe they are students.

The second picture shows a family, probably with children, and they are walking inside a museum.

I think they are looking at an airplane.
questions.sampleB2: Well, at first glance, these two pictures seem quite different. The first one shows three young people, probably young adults, crossing the street at a pedestrian crossing in a European city. They're dressed casually and appear to be enjoying themselves, perhaps heading somewhere. The late afternoon sun gives the scene a pleasant atmosphere. In contrast, the second picture depicts a family – two adults and a young child – walking through an aircraft museum or hangar. They're holding hands and looking at a large plane. Unlike the outdoor urban scene, this is an indoor, educational setting. Both, however, capture people out and about, engaged in leisure activities.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men odamlarni yurganini ko'ryapman.

Bir rasmda ular ko'chada.

Va boshqa rasmda ular muzeyda, menimcha.

Bu katta samolyot.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Rasmlarda men odamlarni ikki xil joyda yurganini ko'rishim mumkin.

Birinchi rasmda ba'zi yoshlar ko'chada yurishibdi, ehtimol ular talabalardir.

Ikkinchi rasmda bir oila, ehtimol bolalari bilan, va ular muzey ichida yurishibdi.

Menimcha, ular samolyotga qarayapti.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Rasmlarda odamlarning piyoda yurgani tasvirlangan, lekin juda boshqa muhitlarda.

Birinchi rasmda bir guruh yoshlar ko'chani kesib o'tayotgani ko'rsatilgan, ehtimol shahar markazida.

Ular xotirjam ko'rinadi va yurish davomida muloqot qilishayotgan bo'lishi mumkin.

Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda bir oilaning aviatsiya muzeyi bo'lib ko'ringan joyda sayr qilayotgani ko'rsatilgan.

Ular katta samolyotni kuzatishmoqda, bu esa ko'proq ta'limiy yoki ko'ngilochar sayohat ekanligini ko'rsatadi.

Asosiy farq ularning yurish maqsadida: biri ehtimol oddiy sayr, ikkinchisi esa qiziqarli joyga qasddan tashrif buyurish.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: a picture is worth a thousand words - "Bir rasm ming so'zga arziydi"
sentenceStarters: "In these pictures, I can see..." - "Bu rasmlarda men ... ko'ryapman"
"The first picture shows..." - "Birinchi rasm ... ko'rsatadi"
"The second picture depicts..." - "Ikkinchi rasm ... tasvirlaydi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In these two pictures, I can see people walking in different settings.
The first picture shows a group of young people, probably students or friends, crossing a zebra crossing on a city street. They appear to be chatting and enjoying each other's company while walking through what looks like a European-style residential area with apartment buildings.
The second picture depicts a family – what appears to be parents with children – walking inside an aviation museum. They're clearly taking in the sights, looking at a large aircraft on display. It's a leisurely stroll with an educational purpose.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki suratda men odamlarning turli xil muhitlarda sayr qilayotganini ko'rishim mumkin.

Birinchi suratda bir guruh yoshlar, ehtimol talabalar yoki do'stlar, shahar ko'chasidagi zebra chizig'idan o'tayotganini ko'rish mumkin. Ular suhbatlashayotganga va bir-birlarining kompaniyasidan zavqlanayotganga o'xshaydi, ular Yevropa uslubidagi turar-joy hududiga o'xshagan joydan, ko'p qavatli uylar orasidan o'tib ketishmoqda.

Ikkinchi suratda esa bir oila – ota-onalar va bolalar bo'lsa kerak – aviatsiya muzeyi ichida sayr qilmoqda. Ular aniqki, ko'rgazmaga qo'yilgan katta samolyotga qarab, diqqat bilan tomosha qilishmoqda. Bu ta'limiy maqsadga ega bo'lgan bemalol sayr.

questions.prompt: Do you like to walk on your own or with others?
questions.sampleA1: I like walk. Alone. It is good.
questions.sampleA2: I like to walk. I like to walk alone. It is quiet. But sometimes I walk with my friend and we talk.
questions.sampleB1: I like to walk. Sometimes I like to walk alone because it's relaxing. I can think. But I also like walking with other people. For example, I walk with my family on Sundays. It's fun to talk and spend time together.
questions.sampleB2: Honestly, it really depends on my mood. When I've had a long day, I much prefer walking on my own — it helps me clear my head and switch off for a bit. But other times, I love strolling with friends, because we can catch up and the time just flies by. So, I suppose I enjoy the best of both worlds.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men piyoda yurishni yaxshi ko'raman. Yolg'iz. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men piyoda yurishni yaxshi ko'raman. Men yolg'iz piyoda yurishni yaxshi ko'raman. U yerda tinch. Lekin ba'zida do'stim bilan piyoda yuraman va biz gaplashamiz.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men piyoda yurishni yaxshi ko'raman. Ba'zan yolg'iz yurishni yaxshi ko'raman, chunki bu dam beradi. Men o'ylashim mumkin. Lekin men boshqa odamlar bilan yurishni ham yaxshi ko'raman.
Masalan, men yakshanba kunlari oilam bilan yuraman. Gaplashish va birga vaqt o'tkazish qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men piyoda yurishni yoqtiraman va yolg'iz yoki boshqalar bilan yurishni afzal ko'rishim vaziyatga bog'liq.

Agar men stressda bo'lsam yoki o'zimga biroz vaqt kerak bo'lsa, yolg'iz yurish juda foydali ekanligini bilaman. Bu menga hech qanday chalg'ituvchi omillarsiz fikrlarimni tartibga solish va qayta ishlash imkonini beradi.

Boshqa tomondan, do'stlar yoki oila a'zolari bilan yurish odamlar bilan muloqot qilish va bog'lanishning ajoyib usuli bo'lishi mumkin. Bu bir-birimiz bilan gaplashib olish va jismoniy mashqlar bilan birga bir-birimizning kompaniyamizdan zavqlanish uchun yaxshi imkoniyatdir.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Do you like to walk on your own or with others?
idioms: If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together - "Tez bormoqchi bo'lsang, yolg'iz bor; uzoq bormoqchi bo'lsang, birga bor"
sentenceStarters: "To be completely honest, I enjoy both..." - "Rostini aytsam, men ikkalasini ham yoqtiraman..."
"When I need to clear my head..." - "Fikrlarimni tozalashim kerak bo'lganda..."
"However, walking with others is equally..." - "Biroq, boshqalar bilan yurish ham..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
To be completely honest, I enjoy both, depending on my mood and purpose.
When I need to clear my head or gather my thoughts, I prefer walking alone. There's something incredibly therapeutic about a solitary walk – it gives me time for self-reflection and helps me decompress after a stressful day.
However, walking with friends or family is equally enjoyable. It's a great opportunity to catch up with loved ones, have meaningful conversations, and strengthen bonds. Walking together makes the time fly by!
As they say, "If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, kayfiyatimga va maqsadimga qarab, ikkalasi ham menga yoqadi.

Agar miyamni tiniqlashtirish yoki fikrlarimni jamlashim kerak bo'lsa, yolg'iz yurishni afzal ko'raman. Yolg'iz yurishda ajoyib davolovchi narsa bor – bu menga o'zim haqimda o'ylashga va stressli kundan keyin dam olishga yordam beradi.

Ammo, do'stlar yoki oila bilan yurish ham xuddi shunday yoqimli. Bu yaqinlar bilan gaplashib olish, mazmunli suhbatlar qurish va aloqalarni mustahkamlash uchun ajoyib imkoniyat. Birga yurish vaqtni tez o'tkazadi!

Aytishlaricha, "Agar tez yurmoqchi bo'lsang, yolg'iz yur; agar uzoqqa yurmoqchi bo'lsang, birga yur".

questions.prompt: Would you say that your city is a good place for walking?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. My city good. Park is good. I walk.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I think my city is good for walking. There are some parks and I like to walk there. But sometimes the cars are too fast and it's a little dangerous.
questions.sampleB1: I think my city is okay for walking. There are some nice places to walk, like the park near my house. However, some streets are very busy and the sidewalks are small. So, it depends on where you are. In my opinion, it could be better.
questions.sampleB2: Well, to be honest, it's a bit of a mixed bag. On the plus side, we've got some lovely parks and a few pedestrian-friendly streets in the centre where you can have a stroll. That said, in a lot of areas the pavements are cramped and the traffic can be a nightmare, so it's not always plain sailing. All in all, there's room for improvement.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Mening shahrim yaxshi. Park yaxshi. Men piyoda yuraman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menimcha, mening shahrim piyoda yurish uchun yaxshi joy. Bir nechta parklar bor va men u yerda yurishni yaxshi ko'raman. Lekin ba'zida mashinalar juda tez yuradi va bu biroz xavfli.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, mening shahrim piyoda yurish uchun yaxshi. Yurish uchun ba'zi bir yaxshi joylar bor, masalan, uyimning yaqinidagi park.
Lekin, ba'zi ko'chalar juda gavjum va yo'laklar kichkina. Shunday qilib, bu qayerda ekanligingizga bog'liq.
Mening fikrimcha, u yaxshiroq bo'lishi mumkin edi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Xo'sh, bu biroz aralash holat, aslida. Bir tomondan, bizda chiroyli yashil maydonlar bor va shahar markazining ayrim joylari piyodalar uchun qulaylashtirilgan. Ushbu joylarda bemalol yoqimli sayr qilish mumkin.

Biroq, hammasi ham gullab-yashnamaydi. Ko'pgina turar-joy hududlarida yo'laklar tor va yomon ta'mirlangan. Qolaversa, transport harakati juda tig'iz bo'lishi mumkin, bu esa piyoda yurishni unchalik yoqimli qilmaydi va ba'zan hatto biroz xavfli ham bo'lishi mumkin. Shunday qilib, uning yaxshi va yomon tomonlari bor.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Would you say that your city is a good place for walking?
idioms: Rome wasn't built in a day - "Rim bir kunda qurilmagan"
stick to the main areas - "asosiy joylarda qolmoq"
sentenceStarters: "I have somewhat mixed feelings about this..." - "Bu borada ikkilanib turaman..."
"On the positive side..." - "Ijobiy tomoni..."
"However, there are significant drawbacks..." - "Biroq, muhim kamchiliklar bor..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Well, I have somewhat mixed feelings about this. Let me explain.
On the positive side, my city has some beautiful parks and pedestrian-friendly zones in the center. There are wide sidewalks in certain areas, and the government has been gradually improving the infrastructure for pedestrians.
However, there are significant drawbacks. Many sidewalks are in poor condition, and some areas lack proper pedestrian crossings. The traffic can be quite chaotic, and not all drivers respect pedestrian rights.
Overall, while there's room for improvement, I'd say it's reasonably good for walking if you stick to the main areas. As they say, "Rome wasn't built in a day" – our city is still developing.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Xo'sh, bu haqda biroz aralash tuyg'ularim bor. Keling, tushuntirib beraman.

Ijobiy tomoni shundaki, mening shahrimda chiroyli bog'lar va markazda piyodalar uchun qulay hududlar bor. Ayrim joylarda keng yo'laklar mavjud va hukumat asta-sekin piyodalar uchun infratuzilmani yaxshilamoqda.

Biroq, sezilarli kamchiliklar ham bor. Ko'pgina yo'laklar yomon ahvolda va ba'zi joylarda piyodalar o'tish joylari yetishmaydi. Transport harakati juda tartibsiz bo'lishi mumkin va hamma haydovchilar ham piyodalar huquqlarini hurmat qilmaydi.

Umuman olganda, yaxshilanishga joy bo'lsa-da, agar siz asosiy hududlarga yopishib olsangiz, piyoda yurish uchun ancha yaxshi deb ayta olaman. Aytishlaricha, "Rim bir kunda qurilgan emas" - bizning shahar hamon rivojlanmoqda.

questions.sampleA1:
I meet people at school.

I like new friends.
questions.sampleA2:
I meet new people at school and at the park.

It is nice because I can play with them.

Sometimes it is difficult, but I try to be friendly.
questions.sampleB1:
I usually meet new people at school or when I'm doing hobbies, like playing football.

I think it's good to meet new people because you can learn new things.

For example, I met a friend who taught me how to play the guitar.

However, sometimes it can be a bit scary talking to someone for the first time.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so I'd like to talk about meeting new people, which is something we all do throughout our lives. To start with, in my country people tend to meet new faces in all sorts of ways. The most common one is probably through friends of friends — someone introduces you at a gathering, and before you know it, you've hit it off. On top of that, university and the workplace are huge, and of course big celebrations like weddings, where dozens of relatives and neighbours all get together. To be honest, we're quite a social bunch, so breaking the ice comes fairly naturally. Moving on to meeting people online — well, I think it's a double-edged sword. On the one hand, it's a brilliant way to connect with like-minded people you'd never bump into otherwise. On the other hand, you really do have to keep your wits about you, because you never quite know who's on the other end. My rule of thumb is to meet in a public place first and not give away personal details too soon. As the saying goes, it's better to be safe than sorry. Finally, do I think friends should spend time together? Absolutely, one hundred percent. The thing is, friendships can easily drift apart if you don't put the effort in. A quick text is fine, but nothing beats meeting up face to face, having a laugh and catching up properly. At the end of the day, that's what really strengthens the bond and keeps a friendship going strong.

bulletPoints: How do people in your country meet new people?
Do you think it's safe to meet new people online?
Do you think it's important for friends to spend time together?
questions.sampleAnswer:
How people meet new people:
In my country, people typically meet new people through several channels. The most common ways include educational institutions like schools and universities, workplaces, and through mutual friends. Traditional gatherings such as weddings, neighborhood celebrations, and religious events also play a significant role in expanding social networks.
Safety of meeting people online:
Regarding online meetings, I believe it can be safe if you exercise caution. It's crucial to verify people's identities, avoid sharing personal information too quickly, and meet in public places first. However, there are definitely risks – cases of catfishing and scams are not uncommon. As they say, "Trust, but verify".
Importance of friends spending time together:
I strongly believe it's essential for friends to spend quality time together. Face-to-face interactions help strengthen bonds and create lasting memories. In our digital age, it's easy to rely on texting, but nothing replaces genuine human connection. "A friend in need is a friend indeed" – and you can only truly be there for someone when you invest time in the relationship.

Odamlar qanday qilib yangi odamlar bilan tanishadi:
Mening mamlakatimda odamlar odatda bir necha yo'llar orqali yangi odamlar bilan tanishadilar. Eng keng tarqalgan usullari maktablar va universitetlar kabi ta'lim muassasalari, ish joylari va o'zaro do'stlar orqali tanishishni o'z ichiga oladi. To'ylar, mahalliy bayramlar va diniy tadbirlar kabi an'anaviy yig'ilishlar ham ijtimoiy tarmoqlarni kengaytirishda muhim rol o'ynaydi.
Odamlar bilan onlayn tanishishning xavfsizligi:
Onlayn uchrashuvlarga kelsak, agar siz ehtiyot bo'lsangiz, bu xavfsiz bo'lishi mumkin deb o'ylayman. Odamlarning shaxsini tekshirish, shaxsiy ma'lumotlarni juda tez ulashmaslik va avvalambor jamoat joylarida uchrashish juda muhim. Biroq, albatta xavflar mavjud – soxta akkauntlar va firibgarlik holatlari kam emas. Aytganlaridek, "Ishon, lekin tekshir".
Do'stlarning birga vaqt o'tkazishining ahamiyati:
Men do'stlarning birga sifatli vaqt o'tkazishi juda muhim deb ishonaman. Yuzma-yuz muloqotlar aloqalarni mustahkamlashga va uzoq muddatli xotiralarni yaratishga yordam beradi. Bizning raqamli davrimizda matnli xabarlarga tayanish oson, ammo hech narsa chinakam insoniy aloqani o'rnini bosa olmaydi. "Do'st og'ir kunda bilinadi" – va siz faqat munosabatlarga vaqt ajratganingizdagina kimdir uchun chin dildan yordam bera olasiz.

questions.prompt: Is it appropriate for adolescents to be sentenced to life without parole?
questions.sampleA1: No. I think no. It is bad. Young people can change.
questions.sampleA2: I don't think it's good. They are young and they make mistakes. Maybe they can be better people later. But it's very bad crime, so I don't know.
questions.sampleB1: I don't really think it's right to give life sentences to young people. They are still growing up and learning. In my opinion, they should have a chance to change their lives. However, it depends on the crime. Some crimes are very serious.
questions.sampleB2: Wow, that's a really weighty question, and to be honest, it's one that splits opinion right down the middle. Let me try to look at both sides. On the one hand, I can see why some people back these sentences. When a teenager commits a truly horrific crime, victims' families understandably want justice, and a life sentence can give them a sense of closure. Supporters also argue it acts as a deterrent — the idea being that if youngsters know they could end up behind bars for good, they might think twice before doing something terrible. From that angle, it's about holding people accountable, no matter their age — in their eyes, the punishment should fit the crime. On the other hand, though, I lean towards the opposite view, and here's why. The thing is, scientists have shown that a teenager's brain, especially the part that controls impulses, simply isn't fully developed yet. So it feels harsh to write off a young person's entire future for a mistake made when they couldn't fully weigh up the consequences. On top of that, these sentences tend to disproportionately affect minority youngsters, which raises serious questions about fairness. And crucially, locking someone up for life rules out any chance of rehabilitation. So, all things considered, I do think serious crimes deserve serious consequences, but I'd argue we should give young people a second chance rather than throwing away the key. As the saying goes, people can change — and at that age, there's still everything to play for.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is an extremely controversial topic that sparks heated debate in legal and ethical circles. Let me present both perspectives.
Proponents of life sentences for adolescents argue that it serves as a powerful deterrent to violent crime. When young people know the consequences are severe, they may think twice before committing heinous acts. Additionally, such sentences can provide a sense of closure and justice for victims' families who have suffered immensely.
However, opponents raise compelling counterarguments. Research shows that adolescent brains are not fully developed, particularly the prefrontal cortex responsible for impulse control and moral reasoning. This means juveniles may not fully understand the consequences of their actions. Furthermore, statistics indicate such sentences disproportionately affect minority youth, raising concerns about systemic bias.
In my opinion, while serious crimes deserve serious consequences, we should consider rehabilitation over punishment for minors. As they say, "Every saint has a past, and every sinner has a future".
